## New: Docker control
A new **Docker** tab (and a Docker card on the Overview) for the Docker host that runs your arr stack:

- **Every container** grouped by compose project, with state, health, uptime, **CPU and RAM**, ports and **update status** – filter by running / stopped / updates and search
- **Start, stop and restart** containers, and read their **logs** (stdout and stderr, auto-refresh, download)
- **Update** a single container or **all** that have updates:
  - the Docker host pulls the new image, then ArrHub recreates the container with the same settings – environment, volumes (named, bind and anonymous), networks and aliases, ports, labels, restart policy – while values that came from the old image are taken from the new one
  - **automatic rollback**: if the new container stops, keeps restarting or reports itself unhealthy, the old one is put back and keeps running
  - containers that share another container's network (e.g. qBittorrent behind a VPN container) are recreated with it
  - images pinned to a digest and ArrHub's own container are left alone; the old image is removed afterwards (optional)
- **Update check** every 6 hours or on demand – done by the Docker host, so ArrHub still never goes to the internet in offline mode

### Setup
Recommended: a **socket proxy** on the Docker host, which gives ArrHub only the Docker API it needs. See [Docker control](https://github.com/moordrak/ArrHub#docker-control) for a ready-to-paste compose snippet, then enter `http://<docker-host>:2375` in **Settings → Docker**. Also supported: `https://host:2376` with TLS client certificates and `unix:///var/run/docker.sock`. Environment variables: `ARRHUB_DOCKER_URL`, `ARRHUB_DOCKER_CERT_PATH` (or `ARRHUB_DOCKER_CA` / `_CERT` / `_KEY`), `ARRHUB_DOCKER_CLEANUP`, `ARRHUB_DOCKER_LINK`.

> Control over Docker means control over the Docker host: turn on the ArrHub login and allow port 2375 only from ArrHub.

## Upgrade

**Docker**
```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/moordrak/arrhub:1.14.0   # or :latest
docker compose up -d                           # if you use docker-compose.yml
```

**Proxmox LXC** (on the Proxmox host)
```bash
pct exec <CTID> -- bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moordrak/arrhub/main/install.sh)"
```

**Debian / Ubuntu**
```bash
bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moordrak/arrhub/main/install.sh)"
```

Your existing `config.json` is kept.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/moordrak/arrhub/compare/v1.13.0...v1.14.0
